zh.title: 華航第三架前四川航空A350 B-18923正式投入服務　CI104首航成田、787-9交付進度再受關注
zh.summary: 中華航空第三架由四川航空轉入的Airbus A350-900、註冊編號B-18923，於10月22日正式投入載客服務，首個營運航班為桃園飛往東京成田的CI104；在A350持續補強運能之際，華航首架787-9仍未交付，最新公開目標仍為年底前接收首批新機。
body: 中華航空機隊再添一架正式投入營運的Airbus A350-900。註冊編號B-18923的A350於今（22）日執行CI104航班，自臺灣桃園國際機場（TPE）飛往東京成田國際機場（NRT），成為該機加入華航後首個載客營運航班，也代表華航自四川航空接收的第三架A350-900開始進入日常航班調度。
B-18923為Airbus A350-941，製造序號MSN 055，前身為四川航空B-304V。公開機隊資料顯示，該機於2016年出廠，2026年5月底退出四川航空營運，完成後續退租與轉手機務作業後轉入華航，並於8月29日以B-18923身分完成交付。連同先前已加入的B-18920與B-18922，華航今年接收的三架前四川航空A350均已陸續納入機隊。
在A350機隊持續補強之際，華航另一項受到高度關注的廣體機更新計畫——Boeing 787-9——交付進度則仍相對落後。華航原先規劃更早接收首架787-9，但時程多次往後調整；華航總經理陳漢銘9月表示，延誤與座椅撞擊測試等認證工作有關，當時仍以2026年底前接收2架787-9為目標，並預計2027年再接收12架。
華航共規劃24架787系列客機，其中包含18架787-9與6架787-10，將作為未來中運量廣體機主力。隨B-18923正式投入載客服務，A350端的新增運能已逐步落地，首架787-9何時完成交付並展開商業營運，也因此再次成為華航機隊更新進度的觀察焦點。截至目前，華航尚未公布較「年底前」更精確的首架787-9交付日期。

en.title: China Airlines Puts Third Ex-Sichuan A350 B-18923 Into Service as 787-9 Delivery Timeline Draws Renewed Attention
en.summary: China Airlines' third Airbus A350-900 transferred from Sichuan Airlines, B-18923, entered passenger service on October 22 with CI104 from Taipei Taoyuan to Tokyo Narita, while the airline's long-delayed first Boeing 787-9 remains pending delivery.
body: China Airlines has placed another Airbus A350-900 into regular passenger service. Aircraft B-18923 operated CI104 from Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport (TPE) to Tokyo Narita International Airport (NRT) on October 22, marking its first revenue passenger flight for China Airlines and bringing the third A350-900 acquired from Sichuan Airlines into day-to-day operations.

B-18923 is an Airbus A350-941 with manufacturer serial number 055 and previously flew for Sichuan Airlines as B-304V. Public fleet records show the aircraft was built in 2016, withdrawn from Sichuan service in late May 2026, and subsequently transferred to China Airlines after return and transition work. It was recorded as delivered to China Airlines on August 29 under its new Taiwanese registration. Together with B-18920 and B-18922, all three former Sichuan A350s acquired this year have now progressively joined the fleet.

The steady addition of A350 capacity contrasts with the slower progress of another key widebody renewal program, the Boeing 787-9. China Airlines had originally expected to receive its first 787 earlier, but the schedule has been pushed back several times. In September, President Chen Han-ming said delays were related in part to seat crash-testing and certification work, while the airline was still targeting delivery of two 787-9s by the end of 2026 and another 12 aircraft in 2027.

China Airlines has planned a 24-aircraft 787 fleet comprising 18 787-9s and six 787-10s, intended to become a core medium-capacity widebody type. With B-18923 now entering passenger service, the airline's additional A350 capacity is already being deployed, putting renewed attention on when the first 787-9 will finally be delivered and begin commercial operations. China Airlines has not publicly provided a more precise delivery date beyond its latest year-end target.
